_note: The building blocks of the HaChi Kyu dishes (see ../dish-details/README.md for how they are used). Each has its name in English, Thai and Burmese (an empty Burmese name means: not translated yet, show the English one), the allergens a typical version of it contains, and whether it is vegetarian. allergens: [] means a typical version has none of the 14 allergens; unknown: true means what is in it is not known (a hidden sauce, a set whose contents are not listed), so a dish that uses it is stored as 'allergens not provided'. basis says where the claim comes from.

sources.S1: Soy sauce is made from soybeans and usually wheat: Soy and wheat (gluten). Several recipe and product pages, e.g. https://www.chopstickchronicles.com/unagi-sauce-recipe/ and gyoza / karaage / miso product labels found by search.
sources.S2: Kabayaki / unagi sauce is soy sauce, mirin, sugar and sake: https://www.napoleon.com/en/us/grills/recipes/unagi-don-japanese-style-grilled-eel-rice and https://www.chopstickchronicles.com/unagi-sauce-recipe/
sources.S3: Tamagoyaki / tamago nigiri: eggs, dashi (bonito stock), soy sauce, mirin, sugar: https://izzycooking.com/tamago-sushi/ and https://1mal1japan.de/en/rezepte/tamagoyaki-made-easy-how-to-make-the-perfect-japanese-omelette-at-home/
sources.S4: Takoyaki: wheat flour, egg, octopus, bonito (fish) and a soy-based sauce, usually with mayonnaise (egg): https://psinfoodservice.com/en/product/3118105-otafuku-takoyaki-sauce-300-g/ and https://yutaka.london/products/frozen/takoyaki-octopus-balls-300g/
sources.S5: Imitation crab (surimi) is fish paste, often with egg white, wheat or other starch and crab extract: https://snacksafely.com/2021/05/like-sushi-avoid-imitation-crab-if-you-are-allergic-to-fish-egg-soy-crustacean-shellfish-potato-wheat-or-corn/ and https://www.bitemybun.com/is-kanikama-imitation-crab-shellfish/
sources.S6: Ikura is salmon roe, typically cured in soy sauce; ebiko is shrimp roe; tobiko is flying-fish roe: https://japanese-products.blog/2018/11/24/tobiko-masago-kazunoko-tarako-ikura and https://www.justonecookbook.com/tobiko-flying-fish-roe/
sources.S7: Karaage: chicken marinated in soy sauce (soy, wheat), coated in potato starch and/or wheat flour: https://www.justonecookbook.com/wprm_print/gluten-free-karaage and https://www.sbs.com.au/food/recipes/easy-karaage-chicken
sources.S8: Yakisoba: wheat noodles, pork, cabbage, a soy / Worcestershire-style sauce (Worcestershire often has fish): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yakisoba and https://www.onceuponachef.com/recipes/yakisoba.html
sources.S9: Gyoza: wheat wrapper, a pork (or chicken) and cabbage filling with soy sauce, garlic, ginger and sesame oil: packaged gyoza labels (Morrisons, Marks & Spencer, Ajinomoto) found by search.
sources.S10: Gochujang is fermented soybean and chilli paste, usually with wheat: https://world.openfoodfacts.org/product/0852320000013/gochujang-korean-chili-sauce-chung-jung-one
sources.S11: Miso soup: miso (soybeans), dashi (bonito, fish), tofu, seaweed, green onion: https://www.huntsfoodgroup.co.uk/?p=255284 and https://yutaka.london/products/miso/bonito-fish-miso-soup-with-toppings/
sources.S12: Addictive cucumber (yamitsuki kyuri / tataki kyuri): smashed cucumber with soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic and sugar: https://okonomikitchen.com/japanese-smashed-cucumber-salad/ and https://www.177milkstreet.com/recipes/addictive-cucumber-salad-yamitsuki-kyuri
sources.S13: Salmon larb / yum: raw or seared salmon, fish sauce, lime, chilli, toasted rice powder, herbs: https://hot-thai-kitchen.com/laab-salmon
sources.S14: Eihire is dried stingray fin, grilled and served with mayonnaise and chilli: https://japanese-products.blog/2021/06/02/eihire and https://rakuzo.dkdining.com/morioka/en/?p=1505
sources.S15: Tontoro / butatoro is a fatty pork cut from the neck (pork jowl or collar), grilled and served on rice with a soy-and-sugar tare: https://therantingpanda.com/2018/05/08/food-review-tokachi-tontaro-at-downtown-gallery-tanjong-pagar-hokkaido-styled-buta-don-from-s11-80-in-cbd/ and https://gigazine.net/gsc_news/en/20100908_sukiya_tontoro
sources.S16: Japan's mandatory allergen labels are egg, milk, wheat, buckwheat, peanut, shrimp, crab and walnut (cashew added in 2026); the recommended ones include squid, salmon, salmon roe, mackerel, sesame, soybean, beef, chicken and pork: https://www.usdajapan.org/wpusda/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/An-Overview-of-the-New-Food-Labeling-Standard_Tokyo_Japan_5-16-2017.pdf
sources.S17: Nam daeng (Thai red soda) is red sala syrup (sugar, flavour, colour E122, preservative) with soda water: https://hungryinthailand.com/nam-daeng-soda-recipe/
sources.S18: Kani miso (crab innards) is the crab's brown paste, sold with crab as the only declared allergen: https://www.sayweee.com/vi/product/Maruha-Nichiro-Crab-Miso-with-Meat-Extreme-Flavor/2871834
sources.S19: General knowledge, not looked up: sushi rice is rice seasoned with vinegar, sugar and salt; tempura batter is wheat flour, egg and water; Japanese mayonnaise has egg; kimchi is made with fish sauce or salted shrimp; Thai basil-and-chilli stir fries use fish sauce, soy sauce and oyster sauce; cola, lemon-lime soda and red soda declare none of the 14 allergens.
